name: Alcovasaurus
isnote: Likely a dacentrurine, and referred to Miragaia by some authors (cited Wikipedia revision); the atlas has no Dacentrurinae clade.
sum: Alcovasaurus is a Late Jurassic stegosaur from the Morrison Formation of Wyoming with very long tail spines, originally named Stegosaurus longispinus.
holotype: UW 20503, a partial postcranial skeleton of an adult with 42 vertebrae, sacrum fragments, ischia, a pubis portion, a femur, ribs and four tail spines — Alcova Quarry, Wyoming.
material: Holotype only; it was damaged in the late 1920s and only a femur is certainly extant.
biology: The very long tail spines are the distinctive feature; no other biology is documented.
author: Galton and Carpenter 2016
